items.title: LTUST Production Wiki
items.text:
This site turns the public La Trobe University Student Theatre (LTUST) production database into a searchable wiki.

Use the search box to find productions by title, people, venue, notes, or other catalogue text. You can also browse by year/month or by category once the wiki pages have been generated from the export.

items.title: Browse
items.text:
• Browse productions by year, month, and undated entries.
  • Browse categories parsed from production metadata.
  • Read the data guide for field and path conventions.
  • Read how to contribute — edit records via pull requests, debate on GitHub Discussions.
  • Read the content notice before reusing archive metadata.

items.title: What is included
items.text: The wiki contains structured catalogue metadata: production titles, dates, venues, abstracts, cast and crew, notes, categories, and source links when those fields are present in the export.

items.title: What is not included
items.text: Programmes, photographs, PDFs, scans, WordPress assets, and other archival media are not redistributed here. When a production page has a source_url, follow it to the original MUST archive entry for more context.

items.title: Rebuilding this site
items.text:
The production and category wiki pages are generated from the source export:

python3 scripts/build_wiki.py
python3 -m zensical build

For local preview, install the docs dependency and run:

python3 -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
python3 scripts/build_wiki.py
python3 -m zensical serve

items.title: Content notice
items.text: This repository contains catalogue metadata about La Trobe University Student Theatre (LTUST) productions, exported for research and reference. It does not redistribute archival materials.

items.title: What is included
items.text: • Structured text fields (title, dates, cast, crew, venue, abstracts, etc.) derived From past students, source urls linked when available

items.title: What is not included
items.text:
• Programmes, photographs, PDFs, or other scanned documents

Where source_url appears in a production file, it points to the web source. Rights in underlying works (scripts, music, images, programmes) remain with their respective creators, not with the MIT license that covers this repository's structure and scripts.

items.title: Contributing to the archive
items.text: Each production page is a curated historical record, not a comment thread. Corrections and debate happen on GitHub so changes stay auditable and can be merged back into the catalogue.

items.title: Edit this page
items.text:
Production wiki pages are generated from source files under productions/. Use Edit this page on any production entry to open the canonical production.md on GitHub and propose a pull request.

Typical pull request changes:

  • Fix typos or formatting
  • Add or correct dates, venues, and credits
  • Add citations in Notes or Materials
  • Link to programs, reviews, or photos hosted elsewhere (see content notice)
  • Optional Media section for URLs that should display inline on the wiki (see data guide)

The build turns supported URLs in Materials, Notes, and Media into embeds that load from the original host — nothing is copied into the repo. Use stable archive links where possible.

Do not edit files under docs/productions/ or docs/categories/ — they are regenerated by python3 scripts/build_wiki.py.

items.title: Discuss this page
items.text:
Use Discuss this page to open a GitHub Discussion about one production without editing the record yet. That is the right place for:

  • Disputed dates or seasons
  • Cast and crew recollections
  • Missing production photographs
  • Conflicting archival sources
  • Oral history from former students and staff

When evidence is clear, someone updates production.md via pull request. The discussion thread remains as provenance.

Discussions use the General category (see wiki.toml). The same category powers the Giscus embed on production pages.

items.title: Pinning a discussion to a page
items.text:
Pre-filled “new discussion” links are used until a thread exists. To link a stable thread number, add an entry to discussions-map.toml at the repo root:

["productions/2017/03/the-light-within-a-night-2017/production.md"]
discussion = 42

Rebuild the wiki after updating the map.

items.title: Contribute material
items.text:
Programs, photographs, and scans are generally not committed to this repository because of copyright. Instead:

  • Open a GitHub issue describing what you have (with your repo URL from wiki.toml once configured), or
  • Post in the relevant Discuss this page thread with links or descriptions of where material can be accessed

Maintainers can then cite external holdings in Materials or Notes.

items.title: Giscus on production pages
items.text: Each production entry shows a Giscus thread below the contribution footer (same General category, pathname mapping). Configuration is in docs/javascripts/giscus.js and wiki.toml ([giscus]). Discuss this page opens the thread on GitHub; the embed shows it inline. Catalogue updates still go through pull requests on production.md.

items.title: Data guide
items.text:
Each production record starts as a Markdown file under productions/.

productions/
  YYYY/
    MM/              # 00 = year known, month unknown
      <slug>/
        production.md
  undated/
    <slug>/
      production.md

The wiki generator creates one page for each production.md file and keeps the same archive path beneath docs/productions/.

items.title: Common fields
items.text:
Production files generally include YAML frontmatter and Markdown sections. Completeness varies across the historical archive.

Common frontmatter fields:

  • title: production title used as the page title.
  • year: production year when known.
  • month: production month when known.
  • date: Production date.
  • source_url: original web source

Common body sections:

  • Date
  • Year
  • Author
  • Produced By
  • Venue
  • Abstract
  • Director
  • Designer
  • Cast
  • Crew
  • Notes
  • Categories
  • Materials
  • Location
  • Media (optional — photos, videos, programmes linked by URL)

items.title: External media embeds
items.text:
List stable URLs in Materials, Notes, or Media (plain URL, Label: URL, or [label](url)). When the wiki is built, known hosts are turned into inline embeds on the generated page; the files stay on the original site (Wayback, Internet Archive, YouTube, and so on).

Supported in v1:

  • Archived images and PDFs on web.archive.org
  • Internet Archive archive.org/details/... items
  • YouTube and Vimeo
  • Direct image URLs (.jpg, .png, .gif, .webp, …)
  • PDFs on other hosts (iframe where allowed)
  • images.humanitix.com (event graphics)

Link only (no iframe): public events.humanitix.com pages, Facebook, Instagram, Issuu, and other hosts that block embedding. For Humanitix checkout on your site, paste the official embed widget src from the Humanitix dashboard into Media — not the public event listing URL.

Prefer Wayback permalinks for longevity. Broken upstream URLs may show empty embeds.

items.title: Generated indexes
items.text:
scripts/build_wiki.py builds:

  • docs/productions/index.md
  • docs/productions/<year>/index.md
  • docs/productions/undated/index.md
  • docs/productions/<year>/<month>/<slug>/index.md
  • docs/categories/index.md
  • docs/categories/<category>.md

Generated pages are ignored by Git so the wiki can be rebuilt from the latest export without editing thousands of derived files.

items.title: Source boundaries
items.text: The generated wiki is a presentation layer over catalogue metadata. Do not add manual edits inside generated production or category pages; edit the source export or the generator instead.

items.title: Contributing corrections
items.text: Each generated production page includes Edit this page (pull request on the source production.md) and Discuss this page (GitHub Discussions). See Contributing for the full workflow, wiki.toml configuration, and optional discussions-map.toml for pinned discussion threads.

items.title: Author
items.text: Devised from the Sundanese tale of Jamarun; directors Sahlan Mujtaba, Bob Pavlich

items.title: Produced By
items.text: Co-production: La Trobe Student Theatre and Film, Mainteater Bandung, Teater Lakon — Asia TOPA 2017

items.title: Venue
items.text: Menzies Theatre, La Trobe University; La Mama Courthouse, Carlton

items.title: Location
items.text: Bundoora and Carlton VIC, Australia; also Bandung and Bali, Indonesia (Feb 2017)

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
Two very different groups of students from neighbouring countries peer into the cultural chasm that divides them. Based on the ancient Sundanese tale of Jamarun — a poor man executed whose corpse is said to take on a beautiful fragrance, drawing birds and butterflies that blot out the sun. Presented through theatre, dance, and multimedia, in multiple languages.

Follows a 1997 co-production with IKIP Bandung (UPI) of Arifin C. Noer's The Bottomless Well.

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
Brighton, 1963. Francis Henshall, a failed skiffle player, has been fired and quickly finds himself employed by two very different masters. Master one: Rachel, disguised as her dead brother Roscoe Crabbe. Master two: Stanley, a posh twit who is both Rachel's lover and her brother's killer. Francis must keep his two guvnors apart — but that is easier said than done.

Richard Bean's adaptation of Carlo Goldoni's A Servant of Two Masters. Part of third-year Bachelor of Creative Arts drama students' end-of-semester performance projects.

items.text: Menzies Theatre, La Trobe University

items.title: Location
items.text: Bundoora VIC, Australia

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
On September 1, 1934 the body of a young woman was found near the Howlong Road, about 8 kilometres out of Albury, NSW. She had been bashed and shot and her body set alight. No one knew who she was — the newspapers named her the Pyjama Girl. In 1944 the woman was identified as Linda Agostini, and her husband Antonio arrested for the murder. But there is much more to the story than the official records suggest. Emma Gibson's research-informed play, framed in the vaudeville era, provides a fresh, theatrical twist.

Part of third-year Bachelor of Creative Arts drama students' end-of-semester performance projects.

items.text: You're on the 86. It's late. You're on the 86 to not be late. It's a CATCH-86. Come join Bush Poet Bill, Pauline Hanson and her (Uluru) rock collection, the Backbench Boys Bill Shorten and Barnaby Joyce, and Hac-Man, your favourite stupol hack, on a journey through La Trobe University via the 86. LTU Revue is a completely original comedy composed of skits and parody songs about La Trobe student life, politics, pop culture, and much more.

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
A party in the 1920s is our window into the lives of New Yorkers and newlyweds Roland and Claire. The play delves into a world of decadence and ruptured mundanity, exploring strained relationships and the pain that comes with having to hide who you are. The production explored LGBTQ+ rights in the 1920s; Rolly, a married and closeted homosexual man, finds acceptance among his gay friends.

(Synopsis quoted from the production's Facebook event, cited in Stage Whispers.)

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
A dramatic drag cabaret written, directed and performed by Tom Cattle for his final university performance. SINNAMANN discusses the obsessions of fame, success and achievement that can arise from pain and torment, and poses consequences for the super ego, which often steps in to protect a damaged soul.

Tom Cattle began drag at 20 as a form of rebellion. Dressing as a woman, he discovered a part of himself he had hidden — able to let go of the barriers and boxes perpetuated as the male 'Tom', transforming into a character that embodies everything from the world.

items.title: Venue
items.text: La Mama Courthouse, 349 Drummond Street Carlton; Menzies Theatre, La Trobe University

items.title: Location
items.text: Carlton and Bundoora VIC, Australia

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
"A sad tale's best for winter…"

Two patriarchs from two royal families, great friends filled with admiration for each other, fall prey to a grave misunderstanding. This leads to an abandoned child, the death of a wrongly accused queen and two decades of guilt and resentment. However, absolution is never too late for those who seek it sincerely!

A cross-cultural collaboration between students from Hong Kong and Melbourne. The first part is set in 1920s colonial Hong Kong; the second in beachside 1970s Australia — a setting chosen to suit the play's movement between two distinct countries and to reflect the cultural diversity of the collaboration.

items.title: Notes

Rehearsals in Hong Kong were cut short in January 2020 due to pro-democracy protests and COVID-19 closures; Hong Kong students travelled to Melbourne earlier than planned to complete the production.

Tired of living in a shallow world that rejects diversity, uni student Uggo plots to dismantle the patriarchy with words. The only things standing in the way of a feminist revolution are Uggo's cute housemate, an impromptu visit from her beauty-influencer sister, and the small matter of actually leaving her flat…

Uggo is a story about self-acceptance, deciding what defines you, and what happens when fear makes all your choices in life.

You. Me. Butterflies. Adoration. Closing blinds. Hands.

In the midst of lockdown, a group of writers from STF formed the Six Lines Project — a weekly writing group that wrote six lines of dialogue in response to a prompt. By the end of 2020, the group had written well over 120 scripts. The Six Lines Showcase stages a small handful of these scripts, with four directors working with a team of actors to bring them to life.

items.title: Author
items.text: Devised by Cole McKenna and Isabelle Piccolo-Cody

items.title: Produced By
items.text: Student Theatre Foundation — Moat 2021

items.title: Venue
items.text: Moat Theatre, La Trobe University

items.title: Location
items.text: Bundoora VIC, Australia (site-specific, roving around campus)

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
I still love you, I don't know what to do.

When do you think you'll love me? Can you text me when you know. Love as possession, the beauty of existence, a threatening beast. How much do you love me? Can you write it on the back of my hand so I don't forget. Love past the end. Love as an always because there is no end.

A site-specific journey around the campus. A theatrical exploration of experiences and impressions of love. Devised by people who love to love, and people who love to do anything but.

It's wondering how much thinking about someone is too much thinking about someone. About learning how to give, and knowing when to stop. It's a foxy Slavoj Zizek making out platonically with a handsome Simone Weil in the middle of a university desperately trying to destroy its creative and liberal arts faculty. It's someone asking you "What do you need?", and for your only response to be "Can you hold me."

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
"That's very beautiful."

Rory and Cora Mulligan; they're starting a new life, on a new land. Their relationship is frayed.

The Blackbird and the Whale; they're old souls to the land. They are watching, learning, and changing.

It's all new and it's intriguing. And now it starts to stir. The weather, the elements, and their emotions: unbalanced. Then the storm hits. They begin to find comfort in new places and pain in the familiar. An exploration of the fine line between love and cruelty, freedom and possession and begs the question why are we so cruel to each other?

"Not really. It ends sadly."

"I can't find the war. I don't know where it is."

There is a war. There are blues and greys. There are priests, protesters… and peas.

Amidst a strange and surreal conflict, a young medical officer scrambles to find her destination — but nobody else seems to know where they're headed either.

Tom Basden's darkly comic miniature epic examines the brutality of war, and the absurd logic of those it sweeps away.

items.title: Notes
items.text: Lakshmi Ganapathy's offstage portfolio lists this production as 2022 (https://lakshmiganapathy.myportfolio.com/theatre). Humanitix lists a La Trobe Student Theatre production on Tue 24 Aug 2021, 8pm, Menzies Theatre, with the same director and overlapping cast (https://events.humanitix.com/there-is-a-war) — consistent with an Activate-season timing. Pinpoint Artists bio also references a 2021 Activate season staging. This record uses year 2022 per portfolio research; reconcile year, season (Moat vs Activate), and exact performance dates against season programs when available. Content warning (from Humanitix): depictions of violence, dead bodies, fake blood, torture, loud noises, war themes. Photo: Mel Viola. Amateur production by arrangement with ORiGiN Theatrical, on behalf of Nick Hern Books.

items.text:
Our journey will now begin.

Here is our protagonist: ordinary, plain, simple, conventional. As is with all of God's other recent creations, this one has been created especially as means of entertainment.

Written in the context of Suharto's 31-year dictatorship, Via Negativa is a strange and satirical exploration of hierarchy, patriarchy, and religion. It is a meeting point of bureaucracy, philosophy, and theology.

items.title: Abstract
items.text:
"Some wines must be taken in context. It's not the wine itself, but its location."

Set over the course of a single night, The Wine List follows Susan Piker (Audrey Page) and Alex Treble (Amaryll Nesbit) as they delve into their troubled high-school partnership. Working through each year bottle by bottle, it is a show about love, accountability and the arduous process of trying to find what we want from our relationships. The Wine List is an entirely original work written and produced at STF.
